newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel little changed vs dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel little changed vs dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose mildly against the dollar but weakened slightly against the basket of foreign currencies in dull trading, dealers said.

"Trading was very quiet and the shekel traded during the day in a very narrow range. The basket traded at around 7.0 percent below the slope and the Bank of Israel was not seen in the market," said Zahi Elias at Bank Leumi.
"Trading was very dull today and activity was very low," said another dealer.

The shekel can trade in a band of seven percent above or below a slope designed to devalue the Israeli currency at six percent a year against a basket of currencies representing Israel's main trading partners.
If the shekel-basket exchange rate reaches the lower trading band the central bank intervenes by buying foreign currency.

The representative rate for the dollar was 3.1680 against 3.1700 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.5502 shekels against 3.5494 on Wednesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8991 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8778 on Wednesday and against the mark at 2.0993 shekels per mark against 2.0973 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.1690 shekels.
